ei.title: 서논술형 Practice2 (Ch5): Metaphors for History / Our Evolving View on Change
ei.subject: 올림포스 영어독해 기본1

fullPassage: We can make literal statements about the past, but without metaphors, we cannot present interpretations of historical facts. Unconsciously, we categorize the data we observe in the world and seek patterns that can be expressed as metaphors. Lakoff and Johnson explain that "We acquire a large system of primary metaphors automatically and unconsciously simply by functioning in the most ordinary of ways in the everyday world from our earliest days." In our common language and common culture, we agree on hundreds of primary metaphors such as "important is big," "happy is up," "similarity is closeness," "difficulties are burdens," "change is motion," "knowing is seeing," "causes are physical forces," and "time is motion." We then blend these primary metaphors to create conceptual metaphors. Working from our sensorimotor domains, we create mental imagery that can be used to interpret subjective experiences, like history. With technology came the idea that innovation and novelty are intrinsic components of civilization. Constant changes in technologies, society, and economics are so ingrained in our daily lives that it is hard to understand that this state of affairs wasn't the rule in the ancient days. A few hundred years ago, change was so slow that most people expected the future to be much like the past. The concept that the future would bring improvements in people's lives was never common, much less popular. All that changed when changes began to occur so often that they were not only perceptible but expected. Since the advent of technology, people expect the future to bring new things that will improve their daily lives. However, many of us now fear that the changes may come too fast, and may be too profound, for normal people to assimilate them.

❌ ③ people expect the future to bring: 'expect + 목적어 + to부정사'로 옳음
❌ ④ to assimilate them: '~하기에는'을 뜻하는 to부정사로 옳음

✅ ④ come too slowly → come too fast: 사람들이 두려워하는 것은 변화가 너무 '빨리(fast)' 온다는 것이므로 slowly는 정반대라 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 우려의 대상 = 변화가 too fast(너무 빨리). too slowly는 반대

questions.passage: We can make literal statements about the past, but without metaphors, we cannot present interpretations of historical facts. Unconsciously, we categorize the data we observe in the world and seek patterns that can be expressed as metaphors. Lakoff and Johnson explain that "We acquire a large system of primary metaphors automatically and unconsciously simply by functioning in the most ordinary of ways in the everyday world from our earliest days." In our common language and common culture, we agree on hundreds of primary metaphors such as "important is big," "happy is up," "similarity is closeness," "difficulties are burdens," "change is motion," "knowing is seeing," "causes are physical forces," and "time is motion." We then blend these primary metaphors to create conceptual metaphors. Working from our sensorimotor domains, we create mental imagery that can be used to interpret subjective experiences, like history. With technology came the idea that innovation and novelty are intrinsic components of civilization. Constant changes in technologies, society, and economics are so ingrained in our daily lives that it is hard to understand that this state of affairs wasn't the rule in the ancient days. A few hundred years ago, change was so slow that most people expected the future to be much like the past. The concept that the future would bring improvements in people's lives was never common, much less popular. All that changed when changes began to occur so often that they were not only perceptible but expected. Since the advent of technology, people expect the future to bring new things that will improve their daily lives. However, many of us now fear that the changes may come too fast, and may be too profound, for normal people to assimilate them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

✅ ③ 우리는 무의식적으로 데이터를 분류하고 패턴을 찾는다: 본문 'Unconsciously, we categorize the data ... and seek patterns'와 일치 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 두 지문의 공통 흐름: 은유는 주관적 경험 해석의 도구이고, 기술은 끊임없는 변화를 당연한 것으로 만듦

❌ ② 은유 없이는 해석이 불가하다고 했으므로 '문자 그대로만'은 틀림
❌ ③ 기술로 변화가 문명의 본질이 되었다고 했으므로 '아무 변화 없음'은 틀림
❌ ④ 은유는 모두가 일상에서 습득한다고 했으므로 '학문에서만'은 틀림

questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 제목 후보 해석 — ① 과거를 잊는 것의 숨은 위험 ② 문자 그대로의 언어가 은유를 이기는 이유 ③ 느린 세계를 위한 고대의 지혜 ④ 은유와 기술이 우리의 사고를 형성하는 방식
det.analysis:
❌ ① The Hidden Danger of Forgetting the Past(과거를 잊는 숨은 위험): 본문은 과거를 잊는 위험을 다루지 않음
❌ ② Why Literal Language Beats Metaphor(문자 언어가 은유를 이기는 이유): 본문은 오히려 은유가 필수라고 함
❌ ③ Ancient Wisdom for a Slow World(느린 세계를 위한 고대의 지혜): 본문은 이제 변화가 빠르다고 함
✅ ④ How Metaphor and Technology Shape Our Minds(은유와 기술이 우리의 사고를 형성하는 방식): 은유로 경험을 해석하는 앞부분과 기술로 변화를 기대·두려워하는 뒷부분을 모두 아우르므로 제목으로 적절 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 not only perceptible but expected가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: not only perceptible but expected = 인지될 뿐 아니라 예상되는 → 변화가 잦아 당연히 일어나리라 여겨짐

❌ ① '눈에 띄지 않아 알아채지 못한다'는 perceptible(인지 가능한)과 정반대
✅ ② 변화가 너무 잦아져 이제는 당연히 일어날 것으로 여겨짐: perceptible(인지됨)을 넘어 expected(예상됨)까지 되었다는 의미와 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ 두려워 피한다는 것은 이 구절의 의미가 아님
❌ ④ '일부 전문가만 감지'는 본문에 없음
det.tip: perceptible(인지되는) → expected(예상되는). 잦은 변화가 당연시됨

questions.passage: __________, but without metaphors, we cannot present interpretations of historical facts. Unconsciously, we categorize the data we observe in the world and seek patterns that can be expressed as metaphors. Lakoff and Johnson explain that "We acquire a large system of primary metaphors automatically and unconsciously simply by functioning in the most ordinary of ways in the everyday world from our earliest days." In our common language and common culture, we agree on hundreds of primary metaphors such as "important is big," "happy is up," "similarity is closeness," "difficulties are burdens," "change is motion," "knowing is seeing," "causes are physical forces," and "time is motion." We then blend these primary metaphors to create conceptual metaphors. Working from our sensorimotor domains, we create mental imagery that can be used to interpret subjective experiences, like history. With technology came the idea that innovation and novelty are intrinsic components of civilization. Constant changes in technologies, society, and economics are so ingrained in our daily lives that it is hard to understand that this state of affairs wasn't the rule in the ancient days. A few hundred years ago, change was so slow that most people expected the future to be much like the past. The concept that the future would bring improvements in people's lives was never common, much less popular. All that changed when changes began to occur so often that they were not only perceptible but expected. Since the advent of technology, people expect the future to bring new things that will improve their daily lives. However, many of us now fear that the changes may come too fast, and may be too profound, for normal people to assimilate them.

다음 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]의 단어를 모두 배열하시오. (영어로)
우리는 과거에 대해 문자 그대로의 진술을 할 수 있다
[보기] about, can, literal, make, past, statements, the, we (8단어)

det.korean: we can make literal statements about the past = 우리는 과거에 대해 문자 그대로의 진술을 할 수 있다
det.analysis: 본문 첫 부분 'We can make literal statements about the past'를 배열합니다. 주어(we) + 조동사(can) + 동사원형(make) + 목적어(literal statements) + 전치사구(about the past) 순서로 놓습니다. 8단어: we / can / make / literal / statements / about / the / past
det.tip: can + 동사원형(make). literal statements = 문자 그대로의 진술 / about the past = 과거에 대해

다음 우리말에 맞도록 빈칸에 들어갈 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로)
